slides.title: Where the prior's stability comes from — and where it does not
bullets: What predicts a gene's score noise? No topology descriptor: degree, k-core, crowding and local density all sit on zero with error bars crossing it.
The noise is the seed sampling itself: RWR weights seeds linearly, so a gene's score is essentially how many seeds are near it -- and bagging the prior over partitions is therefore a provable no-op.
At the rank level a noisy score means a noisy rank (Spearman(rank SD, score CV) = +0.844): a median gene moves ~270 ranks while the arm-level SD stays at 0.0047.
Network-level stability is predicted by coverage and the 2-core fraction (rho = -0.905, q = 0.012) -- not by size, density or modularity.
slides.keyline: the endpoint is stable, the gene is not: the arm-level SD is 0.0047 while the per-gene CV is 18 % and a median gene moves ~270 ranks  |  no topology descriptor predicts a gene's score noise -- degree, k-core, crowding and local density are all on zero  |  the noise is the seed sampling: RWR weights seeds linearly, so bagging the prior is a provable no-op  |  at the network level, coverage and the 2-core predict stability (rho = -0.905)

slides.title: What the benchmark says about network priors
points: A network prior contributes signal beyond node degree
23/24 arms positive; the pre-registered rule met under four of five interval constructions
The contribution is real but modest, and its size depends on the learner

median +0.081 against degree, +0.046 against the strongest classical baseline (closeness), +0.011 under a second locked learner; cleaning the background changes nothing material (23/24 arms, median +0.082)
Much of the published margin is study visibility
a bait-matched null removes most of the enrichment, and the temporal label's advantage collapses to +0.002
gene-level CV is explained by the gene's own score variance (rho = 1.00); bagging the prior is a provable no-op
Curated networks fail on recently discovered drivers
Reactome is +0.089 on the 2019 catalogue and negative on the two newest ones — a coverage and curator-lag effect
One of our three pre-registered hypotheses was never testable
H2 (provenance invariance): 3/1/2 networks per class, and provenance is confounded with size and coverage -- the smallest attainable p-value is 0.1173, so we record it as NOT TESTED
slides.keyline: 1 contributes beyond degree (23/24 arms)  2 but the margin is modest and learner-dependent (+0.081 against degree, +0.046 against the strongest baseline, +0.011 under a second locked learner; the degree baseline is already 0.644, so a 9 % relative gain)  3 much of it is study visibility -- and that part replicates under the second learner (24/24 arms)  4 the instability is intrinsic (rho = 1.00)  5 curated networks fail on recent drivers (Reactome +0.089 on the 2019 catalogue, negative on the two newest)  6 H2 (provenance invariance) was never testable

slides.title: What would change our mind
limits: The gene-cluster interval fails in 4 of 24 arms
run the benchmark on an independent cell-line-derived label (DepMap essential genes) with the same protocol
Our negative set contains curated drivers

SETTLED: with the drivers removed from the background only and the positives untouched, the whole benchmark re-run gives 23/24 arms positive, no sign flips, median +0.0809 -> +0.0822 -- the contamination does not carry the result
The gold standard and the networks share upstream curation
FunMap's gold standard is Reactome-derived and Reactome is a STRING database channel; the training and the test folds are separate (complex-aware CV checks the cross-fold leak)
a blind challenge with a sealed answer key and an expert panel that does not know our method (Boutros et al. 2014)
perturbation experiment: edit the seed set of a driver and measure the effect on the predicted neighbourhood
the increment is learner-specific; degree is not the strongest baseline (closeness wins in 24/24 arms)
run the full degree-preserving rewiring null under the second learner (one arm done: observed +0.0804 vs rewired null -0.0124 +- 0.0072, z = +12.9; the same arm under RWR gives z = +94.2)
3/1/2 networks per provenance class; the smallest attainable p-value is 0.1173
collect more networks: size- and coverage-matched ones, at least four per provenance class -- this is the next thing we are going to do
